links.outcome: Triage accuracy, safety, and overtriage on representative versus standard clinician-authored vignettes
links.effect: Representative vignettes gave higher accuracy (OR 1.52-2.00), higher safety (OR 1.81-3.41), and more overtriage (OR 1.80-2.66); rankings of best SAAs and LLMs changed.
links.quote: We found performance differences in all three groups depending on vignette type: When using representative vignettes, accuracy was higher (OR = 1.52 to 2.00, p < .001 to .03 in binary decisions, i.e., correct or incorrect), safety was higher (OR = 1.81 to 3.41, p < .001 to .002 in binary decisions, i.e., safe or unsafe), and the inclination to overtriage was also higher (OR = 1.80 to 2.66, p < .001 to p = .035 in binary decisions, overtriage or undertriage error).

unlisted_practices: Sampling representative case vignettes from online patient platforms (RepVig framework) for evaluating symptom-assessment applications and LLMs

screen.reason: Empirically tests how the evaluation framework/vignette design practice (representative patient vignettes vs standard clinician-written vignettes) affects measured triage accuracy and safety of LLMs and symptom assessment apps.
